overview.title: Cliffs on the open Atlantic
overview.p1: Cap Beddouza is a headland north of Safi known for cliffs, ocean views and a sense of space far from the medina.
overview.p2: It works well as a half-day trip: transfer, viewpoints, photos and return. There is little urban infrastructure — come prepared.
overview.p3: Pair with a morning in town or a late return for sunset light if timing allows.

food.title: Food around Cap Beddouza
food.p1: Do not count on full services at the cape. Eat in Safi or bring supplies.
food.li1: Picnic if you plan a longer stop.
food.li3: Meal in Safi before or after.
food.li5: Cash only if any seasonal stall appears.
food.p2: Treat Cap Beddouza as a viewpoint outing, not a restaurant destination.

1.title: Arrange transport
1.desc: Taxi or organised transfer. Agree the return before you leave Safi.

2.title: Stay back from edges
2.desc: Cliffs can be abrupt. Keep a safe distance, especially in wind.

3.title: Wind and sun
3.desc: Exposed site — hat, layers and sunscreen help.

q1.question: How far from Safi?
q1.answer: Roughly 25 km north — about a half-hour drive depending on traffic and stops.

q2.question: Is it a full day?
q2.answer: A half-day is enough for most visitors; a full day only if you add other coastal stops.

q4.question: Is it good with children?
q4.answer: Yes for views if you supervise near edges.

q5.question: Do I need a guide?
q5.answer: Not required for viewpoints; useful if you want local coastal context.
